Topic 9.1: LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET & GERMAN ACCENT MARKS
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET & GERMAN ACCENT MARKS, part of GERMAN BRAILLE in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: How do you distinguish letters that are reverse to each other? 2. How do you distinguish the German letters of the alphabet from the English ones?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET & GERMAN ACCENT MARKS together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration – This will be achieved as learners work in pairs and in groups in reading and writing braille.

Self efficacy - Self esteem is developed as learners master the dots forming the alphabet and the German accent marks in Braille.

S) By the end of the sub- strand the learner

should be able to;


a) identify letters of

the alphabet and

the German accent

marks by feeling

and naming the

specific dots that

form them for

knowledge,


b) read out letters of

the alphabet and

the German accent

marks in braille for

learning,


c) write letters of the

alphabet and the

German accent

marks in braille for

skill development.

• Learners could be guided to state the letters

of the alphabet and the German accent marks

in a sequence orally.

• Learners could be guided to identify letters of

the alphabet and the German accent marks by

feeling and naming specific dots that make

each of these characters.

• Learners could be guided to read out the

letters of the alphabet and the German accent

marks on a card.

• Learners could be guided to write the letters

of the alphabet and the German accent marks.

• In pairs learners could practice reading letters

of the alphabet by identifying and reading

letters that are reverse of each other such as

DF, EI, JH, RW.

• In turns learners could practice reading and

writing the German accent marks in braille.

• In groups learners could associate the dots

with letters of the alphabet by singing or

formulating a letter-dot song.
